pc_new: 17 regional SaaS tenants incl. AWS GovCloud and China; PAN-operated control plane
quote: The Prisma Cloud URL indicates the region where your tenant is deployed.
notes: Tenant list includes app.gov.prismacloud.io (us-gov-west-1) and app.prismacloud.cn (Ningxia). PAN blog dated 2024-12-19 (https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/blog/cloud-security/prisma-cloud-achieves-fedramp-high-authorization/) claims FedRAMP High authorization, module scope not stated. Application Security is not listed as available on app.gov, app5 or app.prismacloud.cn (see https://docs.prismacloud.io/content-collections/application-security/application-security). Status stays Limited because the control plane is always PAN-run.

pc_new: SaaS only; Palo Alto Networks runs the console, customer runs Defenders
quote: Palo Alto Networks runs, manages, and updates Compute Console for you. You deploy and manage Defenders in your environment.
notes: No BYOC option is documented for Enterprise Edition. The only self-hosted option is Compute Edition, which covers CWPP only and is out of scope.

pc_new: Defenders run on-prem; the Enterprise Edition control plane is SaaS only
quote: Prisma Cloud is available in two deployment models - SaaS (Prisma Cloud Enterprise Edition) and Self Hosted (Prisma Cloud Compute Edition).
notes: A self-hosted console exists only as Compute Edition (CWPP only, with no CSPM, Application Security or DSPM). Do not cite Compute Edition as an Enterprise Edition capability.

pc_new: Not available for Enterprise Edition; docs direct air-gapped users to Compute Edition
quote: You’re operating in an air-gapped environment.
notes: The quote is a bullet under the heading "When Should You Use Compute Edition?". Compute Edition is self-hosted CWPP only, so no full CNAPP air-gap option exists.

pc_new: Scans VCS repos and CI/CD runs; validates secrets and scans Git history
quote: Application Security scan capability detects secrets in files within your version control system (VCS) repositories and CI/CD executions.
notes: Secrets Security is a separately licensed module. Limit: repositories up to 4GB. Validate Secrets and Scan Git History are optional settings, off by default for validation.

pc_new: Agentless scans find secrets in host and image filesystems; S3 secrets undocumented
quote: Agentless scanning detects sensitive information inside files in your hosts and container images filesystem.
notes: The live claim says cloud storage secrets via data security. DSPM docs (supported-assets, data-types) describe sensitive data classification in S3 and Blob but never name secrets or credentials. The filesystem half is supported (compliance checks 456 and 457). The storage half is unverified, so do not claim S3 secret detection for Prisma, and do not claim a Prisma gap either.

pc_new: Repo scan covers plaintext files; no documented in-cluster ConfigMap secret scan
quote: Prisma Cloud scans any plaintext files that are not encrypted, not compressed
notes: No Enterprise Edition page mentions ConfigMaps. ConfigMap YAML in a repo falls under generic plaintext secrets scanning. Runtime checks cover image and container environment variables (checks 424 and 597), not live ConfigMaps. The live phrase "limited to compliance checks" has no source.

pc_new: SCA with SBOM inventory, license compliance and PR-based package fixes
quote: provides a comprehensive inventory of third-party dependencies detected in your environment, including vulnerabilities and security insights.
notes: SCA is a separate module. SCA skips dev and test dependencies (supported-technologies page). Runtime SBOM export also exists at runtime-security/vulnerability-management/exporting-sboms. The live cell adjective "Comprehensive" is removed in pc_new.

pc_new: Scans IaC, SCA, secrets and CI/CD risks; no code quality scanning documented
quote: identifying cloud infrastructure misconfigurations and vulnerabilities across IaC, SCA , Secrets, as well as CI/CD risks in the pipeline.
notes: No maintainability or code-quality feature appears in the Application Security docs tree. SonarQube ingestion imports SAST findings only.

pc_new: Terraform, OpenTofu, CloudFormation, ARM, Bicep, K8s, Helm, Kustomize, Ansible, SAM, Dockerfile
quote: Prisma Cloud Application Security supports the following technologies and frameworks.
notes: Full IaC list on the page: ARM, Bicep, CloudFormation, Dockerfile, Helm, Kubernetes, Kustomize, OpenAPI, OpenTofu, Serverless Framework, AWS SAM, Terraform, Terraform Plan, Ansible. The live cell lists four and uses a dash icon. pc_new is 12 words.

pc_new: Registry, image and CI image scanning via Defenders, agentless and twistcli
quote: Configure Prisma Cloud to scan your registries.
notes: Registries listed: Sonatype Nexus, Alibaba ACR, ECR, ACR, Docker v2, GitLab, GAR, GCR, Harbor, IBM, JFrog Artifactory, OpenShift, CoreOS Quay. Application Security also lists container image scanning.

pc_new: Ingests SARIF 2.0 and 2.1 files via console or API
quote: Prisma Cloud supports SARIF versions 2.0 and 2.1 and accepts `.zip`, `.json`, and `.sarif` files.
notes: The live cell says no native SARIF ingestion. That claim is wrong and must change. SARIF findings map to onboarded repositories only and appear as code weaknesses. Native Veracode and SonarQube ingestion also exist.

pc_new: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure Repos, CodeCommit; Jenkins, Actions, CircleCI, Azure Pipelines
quote: Integrate Prisma Cloud with your CI/CD runs in order to scan and detect misconfigurations in your infrastructure-as-code (IaC) files
notes: VCS list from https://docs.prismacloud.io/content-collections/application-security/get-started/connect-code-and-build-providers/code-repositories : AWS CodeCommit, Azure Repos, Bitbucket, Bitbucket Server, GitHub, GitHub Server, GitLab, GitLab Self-managed. CI/CD runs add AWS CodeBuild, GitLab Runner, Checkov, Terraform Cloud and Enterprise. Pipeline scans cover IaC, SCA, secrets and license only, with no SAST or DAST.

pc_new: No native SAST scanner documented; ingests SAST findings from Veracode, SonarQube, SARIF
quote: By ingesting static application security testing (SAST) findings from supported third-party tools, Prisma Cloud consolidates and enriches your security vulnerability data
notes: Searched the Application Security docs tree and all 81 Enterprise Edition release-note pages (2023 to Aug 2026): no native SAST scanner. The live cell ticks SAST. Native SAST is marketed under Cortex Cloud Application Security, which is out of scope. pc_new is 12 words.

pc_new: No DAST capability in Enterprise Edition docs; WAAS is runtime protection
quote: covering the entire software development lifecycle from code to cloud including Infrastructure as Code (IaC) security, Software Composition Analysis (SCA), Secrets Security, CI/CD pipeline security
notes: No DAST page exists in the Enterprise Edition docs index (https://docs.prismacloud.io/llms.txt) or release notes. WAAS is a runtime WAF and API protection, not a DAST scanner.
